In 2017, Bray N, Noyes J, Edwards RT, and Harris N conducted a mixed-method systematic review and developed a conceptual framework focusing on wheelchair interventions, services, and provision for disabled children. This study was published in Disability and Rehabilitation: Assistive Technology. 2. In 2014, Graham F, Boland P, Grainger R, and Wallace S performed a scoping review on the use of telehealth for remote assessment of wheelchair and seating needs for both adults and children. Their findings were published in BMC Health Services Research. 3. In 2020, Graham F, Boland P, Wallace S, Taylor WJ, Jones B, Maggo J, and colleagues explored the social and technical readiness for a telehealth assessment service designed for adults with complex wheelchair and seating needs. This study included a national survey of stakeholders and was published in Disability & Rehabilitation. 4. In 2016, Salatino C, Andrich R, Converti RM, and Saruggia M conducted an observational study on the provision of powered wheelchairs in Italy. Their research was published in Assistive Technology. 5. In 2022, Gowran RJ, Clifford A, Gallagher A, McKee J, O’Regan B, and McKay EA examined wheelchair and seating assistive technology provision as a gateway to freedom. Their study was published in Disability and Rehabilitation. 6. In 2007, Armstrong W, Reisinger KD, and Smith WK evaluated the CIR-Whirlwind wheelchair and its service provision in Afghanistan. Their findings were published in Disability & Rehabilitation. 7. In 2016, Toro ML, Eke C, and Pearlman J investigated the impact of the World Health Organization's 8-step wheelchair service provision model on wheelchair users in resource-limited settings. This cohort study, conducted in Indonesia, was published in BMC Health Services Research. 8. In 1997, Beaumont-White S and Ham RO questioned whether powered wheelchairs enable or disable users. Their study was published in Prosthetics & Orthotics International. 9. In 1997, Post MWM, Van Asbeck FWA, Van Dijk AJ, and Schrijvers AJP assessed the availability of and satisfaction with services for individuals with spinal cord injuries. Their research was published in Spinal Cord. 10. In 2021, D'Innocenzo ME, Pearlman JL, Garcia-Mendez Y, Vasquez-Gabela S, Zigler C, Rosen P, and colleagues conducted an exploratory investigation into the outcomes of wheelchair provision through two service models in Indonesia. Their findings were published in PLoS ONE. 11. In 2016, Visagie S, Mlambo T, Van der Veen J, Nhunzvi C, Tigere D, and Scheffler E studied the impact of structured wheelchair services on user satisfaction and functionality in Zimbabwe. Their research was published in the African Journal of Disability. 12. In 2017, Williams E, Hurwitz E, Obaga I, Onguti B, Rivera A, Sy TRL, and colleagues conducted a qualitative study on the perspectives of basic wheelchair users in Kenya and the Philippines regarding improved access to wheelchair services. Their findings were published in BMC International Health & Human Rights. 13. In 2000, Suzuki KM and Lockette G conducted a client satisfaction survey of a wheelchair seating clinic. Their study was published in Physical and Occupational Therapy in Geriatrics. 14. In 2006, Verza R, Lopes Carvalho ML, Battaglia MA, and Messmer Uccelli M demonstrated that an interdisciplinary approach to evaluating the need for assistive technology reduces equipment abandonment. Their research was published in Multiple Sclerosis.
